name.text: Is the given line a line of symmetry?

questiontext.text:
The dashed line is drawn on the shape below.

Decide whether the dashed line is a line of symmetry of the shape. (A line of symmetry divides a shape into two halves that are exact mirror images of each other.)

generalfeedback.text:
{@reasonTxt@}

The orange shape below is the original reflected in the dashed line. It is a line of symmetry exactly when the orange copy lands back on the original.

[[jsxgraph height='400px' width='460px']] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-2, 12, 16, -2], keepaspectratio: true, axis: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: { enabled: false }, zoom: { enabled: false } }); var V = {#worldV#}; var A = {#lineA#}; var B = {#lineB#}; var pts = V.map(function (c) { return board.create('point', c, { visible: false, fixed: true }); }); board.create('polygon', pts, { fillColor: '#9467bd', fillOpacity: 0.30, borders: { strokeColor: '#6a3d9a', strokeWidth: 3 }, fixed: true, vertices: { visible: false } }); board.create('line', [A, B], { strokeColor: '#d62728', dash: 2, strokeWidth: 2, straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, fixed: true }); // Reflection of the shape in the dashed line var mirror = board.create('line', [A, B], { visible: false }); var refl = board.create('transform', [mirror], { type: 'reflect' }); var rpts = pts.map(function (P) { return board.create('point', [P, refl], { visible: false }); }); board.create('polygon', rpts, { fillColor: '#ff7f0e', fillOpacity: 0.25, borders: { strokeColor: '#ff7f0e', strokeWidth: 2, dash: 2 }, fixed: true, vertices: { visible: false } }); board.renderer.svgRoot.style.pointerEvents = "none"; [[/jsxgraph]]

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

falsefeedback.text: Not quite. A line is a line of symmetry only if folding the shape along it makes the two halves land exactly on top of each other — every point matching its mirror image, and the line passing through the middle of the shape. Look again: are the two sides really mirror images, and does the line pass through the centre?

qtest.description: Opposite (wrong) decision routes to the teaching feedback.
